question: Do these synthetic traces satisfy the proposed command arbitration rules?
limits: All observations and dispatches are synthetic.
No native field, manual-order hook, transport, game identity or runtime behavior is established.
The model rejects writes when manual-order observation is unknown.
Single actor/action, single model-owned clock, no concurrency or process/network behavior tested.
Ledger/queue sizes and timing values are evaluation settings, not production performance claims.

results.title: Fresh explicitly armed single-AI intent reaches only mock dispatch
No implicit arming
Unknown manual observation cannot be treated as generation zero
Fractional manual generation is not usable evidence
Human order between receipt and dispatch cancels queue despite rearm
Identical queued and dispatched duplicates never dispatch again
Reusing an ID with an altered binding rejects the collision
Old-session queue and replay cannot survive mission rotation
A new occupant in the selected slot invalidates the old command
Human possession revokes a queued AI command
Destroyed pawn revokes a queued command
Pause and resume cannot resurrect queued work
Unknown authority at dispatch cancels queued work
IPC disconnection and reconnection require explicit rearm
TTL expires at the exact first-receipt deadline
Retransmission does not extend the original deadline
Fresh receipt cannot renew an old telemetry observation
Future synthetic sample times are invalid
Snapshot context must still match at dispatch
Explicit rearm cannot bypass the two-second rate limit
Fresh command may dispatch at the exact cooldown boundary
A third queued command is rejected at capacity
Ledger saturation disarms without evicting a rejected command ID
Unconfirmed outcome never produces automatic retry or acceptance
Unsupported attack action is rejected before queueing
Extra target or arbitrary payload field is rejected
Wrong primitive types cannot impersonate a valid command
Oversized supplied text is rejected as data
Manual revision must match even with a fresh snapshot
Missing native capability rejects every write
An explicitly refreshed new session can use a local ID again
A sequence regression revokes already queued work
A fresh command immediately before TTL remains eligible
A backwards model clock is a fixture error, never an age reset
Replayed snapshot time cannot freshen old queued intent or support rearm
Manual revision rollback cannot become the baseline on explicit rearm
A reused epoch cannot clear the ledger and make old traffic new
Pause cannot hide manual rollback or permit rearm from retained state
Rejected future sample cannot mature into permission as time catches up
Unknown manual observation retains the prior revision high-water mark
Fault recovery requires a fresh newer valid observation and explicit rearm
Pause cannot hide a sample-time rollback behind a newer sequence
New epoch cannot inherit authority or mission readiness from the prior world
Wrong actor with otherwise matching generation is rejected directly
Unknown actor binding cannot be armed or inferred from the command
